turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi there, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Victor Petrov.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Before we get going,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Rodrigo Esquivel, January 30, 1982.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Rodrigo. And is your address still the one on Kellogg Avenue?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, we moved in July. It's 905 Magnolia Terrace now. Got it, I'll update that. So, Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Lindqvist sent you to us about your blood pressure. What's the story?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So, at my physical in July it was high, like 156 over 98. She had me check it at home, and it's been running in the 150s over 90s pretty much every day for two months.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And she started a medicine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, amylodipine 5 mg once a day.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: About 6 weeks ago.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It came down a little, but my readings are still like 145 over 92. too. Any headaches,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: vision changes, or chest pain.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No headaches, visions fine, no chest pain.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Shortness of breath or swelling in your legs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No neither. Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Lindfist wrote that you're worried because of your family.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Tell me about that. Yeah, that's honestly why I'm here. My dad had a heart attack at 51 and he passed away from a second one at 58, and my mom had a stroke when she was 70, so I'm kind of freaking out about this. I'm sorry about your dad.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's a real reason to take this seriously and we will. Have you ever had any heart problems yourself? Any chest pain or a heart test?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No nothing, never had any heart issue, just the blood pressure.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay do you snore?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My wife Danny Ellis says I snore like a chainsaw. She says sometimes I stop breathing and then gasp.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm tired most days too. That's important, I'll come back to it. Any medicines over the counter, decongestants, pain relievers.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take pseudoephedrine most mornings for my sinuses, 30 milligrams, maybe two tablets.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Alcohol smoking.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Three or four beers on the weekend, I've never smoked. I'm a project manager at Brightwater Construction so I eat a lot of fast food on the road if I'm being honest.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks for being straight with me. Let me check you. Your blood pressure is 148 over 94 in the right arm, 144 over 90 in the left. I repeated it after five minutes and got 146 over 92. Pulse 80. Weight is 228 pounds, which puts your BMI at 31 .4. No brutes in your neck or belly. Heart is regular, no murmurs. Lungs are clear, no legs swelling, and the pulses in your groin and feet are normal.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I also looked at the labs and ECG doctor. Linkvist sent. Kidney function is normal. Create 9 1 .0, potassium 4 .1, and ura 1c is 5 .6, so no diabetes. The ECG from August shows sinus rhythm with some voltage that suggests the heart muscle may be a little thick from the pressure.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thick is that bad?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It's a sign the blood pressure has been working the heart harder and it's very treatable. So my thinking is this. You have high blood pressure that isn't controlled yet. To be clear,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: you haven't had a heart attack or a stroke,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: those were your parents. But your family history does raise your risk, so we want to get your numbers down and look at the whole picture.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, that helps. First,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm increasing the amylolipine to 10 mg once a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Second,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: please stop the pseudoephedrine, it pushes the blood pressure up. Use a fluticasone nasal spray instead, two sprays in each nostril once a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I didn't know that about the decongestant.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Most people don't.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Third,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: the snoring and stopping breathing sound like sleep apnea, which is a common cause of hard to control blood pressure. I'm ordering a home sleep study. I also want an echocardiogram to look at the heart muscle and a fasting lipid panel and a urine test for protein.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: On the lifestyle side, try to keep salt under 2000 mg a day and cut back to no more than one or two beers at a time. Keep checking your blood pressure at home twice a day and bring the log in your cuff next time. We'll do, should I worry about chest pain like my dad? If you ever get chest pain,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: sudden weakness,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: or trouble speaking,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: call 911 right away.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Otherwise I'll see you back in four weeks to go over the tests and your home numbers.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good, thanks doctor.
